en.name: Root Canal Therapy
en.meta_title: Root Canal Therapy: Saving an Infected Tooth from Extraction
en.meta_description: Relieve severe tooth pain and save an infected tooth with gentle, effective root canal therapy. Learn how this procedure removes infected pulp to prevent abscesses and preserve your natural tooth.
en.meta_keywords: root canal therapy, infected tooth, tooth pain relief, endodontic treatment, save a tooth, dental abscess, restorative dentistry

what_is.heading: What is Root Canal Therapy? Saving an Infected Tooth
paragraphs: Save a severely infected or inflamed tooth from extraction with our gentle and effective Infected Teeth Treatment, more commonly known as root canal therapy. This crucial procedure is necessary when the soft tissue inside the tooth, called the pulp, becomes infected due to deep decay, repeated dental procedures, or a crack in the tooth.

why_needed.heading: Why is a Root Canal Necessary?
paragraphs: If left untreated, an infected pulp can cause severe pain, an abscess, and eventually the loss of the tooth. Root canal therapy involves carefully removing the infected or inflamed pulp from inside the tooth and its root canals.

procedure.heading: The Procedure: Cleaning and Sealing
paragraphs: Once the pulp is removed, the inside of the tooth is meticulously cleaned, disinfected, and then filled and sealed. The procedure is performed under local anesthesia and is typically no more uncomfortable than getting a regular filling. After a root canal, it is usually recommended to place a crown on the tooth to protect it from fracture and restore it to full function. This therapy is a vital tool for relieving dental pain and preserving your natural teeth.
